segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics news digest for October 7th, 2026.
Today we cover major moves from Boston Dynamics, exciting advancements in collision-free planning, and a fascinating look at rapid robot building.
From Humanoids Daily, Boston Dynamics has named former Amazon AI leader Rohit Prasad as Chief Executive Officer, effective October 7, to drive the commercialization of its robotic systems.
This appointment signals a strategic focus on integrating advanced artificial intelligence into the company's robotics portfolio.

Boston Dynamics is leveraging Prasad's background in Amazon AI, where he contributed to Alexa and the Nova foundation models, to steer the development of its robotic systems, including Spot, Stretch, and Atlas.
This move is intended to advance the application of sophisticated AI capabilities across industrial and commercial settings.
The transition follows a period of organizational change within the company's leadership structure.
This development indicates a growing trend of applying large-scale AI expertise to physical robotics for real-world deployment.
From MIT News - Robotics, "Planning system ensures a robot’s flight path will remain collision-free".
This report details the development of a method to plan flight paths for unmanned aerial vehicles that avoid unknown, moving obstacles.
Researchers developed a system named SANDO which mathematically guarantees collision-free routes through unmapped environments, even when obstacles move unpredictably.
The system achieves this by creating a time-sensitive safety corridor by considering the future movements of dynamic obstacles based on their maximum velocity.
It utilizes heat-map techniques and optimizes trajectories to ensure the fastest, safest path while enabling rapid onboard replanning.
This methodology provides formal safety guarantees crucial for high-stakes operations such as search and rescue missions.
This advancement establishes a framework for reliable autonomous navigation in dynamic, unknown settings.
From Robohub, "What three days building a robot taught me"

details an experience at the UK RAS STEPS MicroMaze Robot Hackathon where participants constructed an autonomous robot to navigate progressively complex mazes, revealing that the most valuable outcomes were the unexpected relationships forged during the building process.
During the three-day event, participants assembled small autonomous robots utilizing components such as sensors, motors, and a Raspberry Pi Pico W.
The process involved debugging the system to successfully navigate the increasingly difficult maze challenges.
Beyond the technical execution, the activity facilitated strong team friendships and provided an opportunity for networking within York.
This experience underscored that collaborative building yields significant social outcomes alongside technical achievements.
The focus on collaborative engineering points toward the importance of team development in advancing the artificial intelligence and technology industry.
And that’s all the circuits we have for today!
From algorithms to ambition, hope your day is fully optimized.
Until tomorrow, keep coding your world.
See you then!
